claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a nanocrystalline, chemically homogeneous microstructure.
Overall wear resistance under high-temperature sliding is governed by an adherent protective copper oxide layer.
Microscopic deformation under high-temperature sliding is governed by the copper oxide layer.
Controlled annealing promotes Cu segregation to grain boundaries in FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Grain-boundary-segregated Cu preferentially oxidizes during high-temperature sliding.
Oxidation of segregated Cu produces a continuous, adherent Cu oxide layer at the surface and along grain boundaries.
The Cu oxide film is lubricious and protective.
The Cu oxide film reduces direct asperity or metal-to-metal contact.
The Cu oxide film inhibits dislocation-mediated plastic deformation.
The Cu oxide film inhibits grain-boundary-mediated plastic deformation.
Formation of the Cu oxide film lowers friction and wear.
Annealed coatings should have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings.
Annealed coatings should have lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings.
Annealing should shift microscopic deformation away from dislocation-dominated deformation toward behavior mediated by the protective oxide layer.
The as-deposited baseline should exhibit less Cu segregation than the annealed coating.
The as-deposited baseline should exhibit less Cu oxide formation than the annealed coating.
The proposed regime is ambient-atmosphere sliding at approximately 300 °C and above.
Oxidation reactions are sufficiently active at approximately 300 °C and above to enable the proposed Cu oxide mechanism.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction depends on the degree of Cu segregation and the quality of the oxide film.
Failure to obtain Cu oxide enrichment, reduced friction and wear, or a deformation-mechanism shift is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
